circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit, designed by Hermann Tilke and located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. Spanning 5. 281 kilometers, it represents one of four Middle Eastern Formula One circuits, following Bahrain and preceding tracks in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling a lake in Melbourne that hosts the Australian Grand Prix as its premier motorsport event. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates multiple racing series including local touring car competitions alongside the Formula One championship.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit originally operated as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following substantial modifications and a name change, the track resumed hosting the Grand Prix from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street racing venue in Azerbaijan's capital, situated along Baku Boulevard, with a lap distance of 6. 003 km that ranks as the fourth-longest on the Formula One schedule. The circuit first hosted an F1 race in 2016 as the European Grand Prix, before becoming the permanent home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix held in the Middle East, and continues to stage the annual Bahrain Grand Prix alongside various motorsport categories including GP2 racing and endurance events. The FIA Grade 1 facility features multiple circuit configurations and has previously accommodated touring car racing.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish motorsport facility features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a comprehensive test of driver and car performance. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its stands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Spa-Francorchamps is a 7. 004 km Belgian racing circuit situated near the town of Spa in Wallonia, currently hosting the Formula One Belgian Grand Prix. The venue has maintained continuous Grand Prix racing since 1985, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006, having originally staged its first race in 1925 and participated in the inaugural F1 world championship season in 1950.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km temporary road course that serves as the home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond its use in motorsport's premier category, the venue has hosted various international racing series including sports car championships, open-wheel competitions, and NASCAR events.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this Chinese motorsport venue hosted the country's Formula One grand prix annually between 2004 and 2019, before resuming the event from 2024. The circuit has expanded its motorsport calendar to include electric racing competitions in recent years.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near villages in Northamptonshire, Silverstone Circuit hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950 and has served as the primary home of the British Grand Prix since 1987, following decades of rotation with other English tracks. The venue additionally stages the British round of motorcycle racing's premier series.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, a 4. 381 km circuit near Budapest in Mogyoród, hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix held behind the Iron Curtain in 1986, marking a historic expansion of the sport into Eastern Europe. Constructed in just eight months starting in late 1985, the purpose-built venue was chosen over a proposed street circuit alternative and remains the fastest-built Formula One track on record.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza, located near Milan in Italy, is a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venue. It has hosted the Italian Grand Prix annually since 1949 (except during 1980 renovations), making it one of the few tracks to appear on every Formula One calendar since the championship's inception, and earned the nickname "Temple of Speed" for its fast-flowing layout featuring extended straights and quick corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km track in Mie Prefecture, Japan, operated by Honda Mobilityland with a capacity of 155,000 spectators. The venue hosts major motorsport competitions, most notably the Formula One Japanese Grand Prix and the Super Formula championship.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, adjacent to Las Vegas, weaving around the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its collection of major hotel and casino properties. The track passes iconic venues including MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, creating a racing environment integrated with the city's most recognizable attractions.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is named after two Mexican racing brothers who died in motorsport accidents during the 1960s and early 1970s. The circuit has returned to hosting Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix since 2015 on its current layout, resuming a tradition last held in 1992 on a different configuration.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 turns and qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One, the venue has hosted the Miami Grand Prix since joining the championship calendar in 2022, while also hosting electric racing series from 2025 onward.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street course that winds through Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, circling the harbour area of the Principality of Monaco. The track is widely known as Monte Carlo, reflecting that much of its layout occupies the Monte Carlo neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the Dutch Grand Prix after rejoining the Formula One calendar in 2021. The venue's association with the sport concluded following the 2026 season.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a purpose-built racing venue situated north of Doha in Qatar, spanning 5. 419 kilometers with a notably lengthy 1. 068-kilometer main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km racing circuit in São Paulo, Brazil, which opened in 1940 and was later renamed in 1985 to commemorate the late Formula One driver José Carlos Pace. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and hosts a karting facility dedicated to another celebrated Brazilian racing driver.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street-based racing venue positioned along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coastline, serving as the home of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix in Formula One since 2021.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through downtown Singapore around the Marina Bay waterfront, incorporating sections of the Downtown Core and Kallang planning districts into its urban layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya stretches 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced design with extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing multiple racing disciplines. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located near Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 FIA track that serves as the permanent home for the United States Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the facility has hosted various motorsport championships including MotoGP, NASCAR, World Endurance Championship events, and previously accommodated IndyCar and sports car racing series.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British driver competing in Formula One for Williams under Thailand's flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, having secured two world championships during his 23-season career with 32 Grand Prix victories. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso achieved notable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans 24 Hours triumphs with Toyota and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to have won both Formula One and World Endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli represents Mercedes in Formula One, where he has claimed eight race victories following his entry into the sport in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas in the sport's top championship series.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto competes in Formula One as part of the Audi team. Bortoleto has established himself as a professional racing competitor at the sport's highest level.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Bottas is a Finnish Formula One driver currently racing for Cadillac who has secured two runner-up finishes in the World Drivers' Championship during his tenure with Mercedes. Over his 13-season career, he has achieved 10 Grand Prix victories.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto, an Argentine racing driver, currently competes in Formula One as a member of the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan holds a reserve position with Haas while pursuing his endurance racing career in the European Le Mans Series with Nielsen Racing in the LMP2 category. Between 2024 and 2025, he made seven Formula One race starts.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The driver achieved a notable victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix during his previous tenure with AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Hadjar is a French-Algerian Formula One driver currently racing for Red Bull Racing under the French banner.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton, a British driver, currently races for Ferrari in Formula One and has achieved seven world championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record. He also holds multiple performance records in the sport, including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium appearances.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: Nicolas Hülkenberg is a German Formula One driver currently competing for Audi. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved significant success in endurance racing, notably claiming victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a driver from Monaco, races for Ferrari in Formula One and has secured nine race victories throughout his nine-season career. He finished as the championship runner-up in 2022 while driving for the Scuderia.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver who currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship for BMW, while also participating part-time in NASCAR's top series. His Formula One career, which spanned from 2014 to 2020 and again from 2022 to 2024, has now concluded as he focuses on endurance racing and stock car competition.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: British driver Lando Norris achieved the pinnacle of motorsport success by clinching the 2025 Formula One championship while competing for McLaren. Over his eight-season career in the sport, he has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The driver previously achieved a grand prix victory with Alpine at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez currently races for Cadillac in Formula One after spending 15 seasons in the sport and claiming six race victories. He finished as runner-up in the 2023 drivers' championship while competing for Red Bull.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri competes for McLaren in Formula One, having accumulated nine race victories throughout his four seasons in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: An Australian driver who raced in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, Ricciardo earned the nickname "the Honey Badger" during his career and secured eight Grand Prix victories throughout his time in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell competes for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured seven Grand Prix victories over the course of eight seasons.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Carlos Sainz, a Spanish motorsport competitor, currently drives for Williams in Formula One competition. Throughout his 12-year career in the sport, he has secured victories in four Grand Prix races.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant, an American driver, raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to endurance racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, following prior experience in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Canadian driver Lance Stroll currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, competing at the highest level of international motorsport.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Japanese driver Yuki Tsunoda transitioned to a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls after five seasons as a full-time Formula One competitor from 2021 through 2025, stepping back to support duties in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch and Belgian driver Max Verstappen has secured four consecutive Formula One World Drivers' Championships between 2021 and 2024 while racing for Red Bull Racing under the Dutch flag. Across his 12-season career, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu represents China in motorsport as a reserve driver for the Cadillac Formula One team. The racing driver competed in the championship between 2022 and 2024, holding the distinction of being the sole Chinese competitor to have participated in the sport at this level.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based Alpine team has competed in Formula One since 2021, when Renault rebranded its long-standing works operation to promote its Alpine sports car division. The French manufacturer operated the squad through the Renault-Nissan-Mitsubishi Alliance before withdrawing from the sport at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has maintained a presence in Formula One across multiple eras, with its present iteration operating as AMR GP Limited and competing under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, is Formula One's longest-established and most accomplished team, competing continuously since the championship's inception in 1950. The squad, colloquially called "the Prancing Horse" after its iconic emblem, remains the only team to have participated in every World Championship season.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American Formula One team in 2014, with the squad entering the championship in 2016. Currently led by team principal Ayao Komatsu following Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024, the outfit competes under the TGR Haas F1 Team banner.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: This Swiss engineering firm, established by Peter Sauber in 1970, built sports cars and racing machinery before joining Formula One in 1993. The outfit achieved notable success in endurance competition, including a Le Mans victory in 1989, though it underwent numerous transformations during its 32-year F1 tenure before ceasing operations in 2025 as one of motorsport's most enduring independent constructors, subsequently becoming Audi's technical foundation for their championship ambitions.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its Woking facility, operating as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group under Mumtalakat Holding Company's ownership.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has been a significant Formula One participant since 1954, operating as both a constructor and engine supplier. The current team, Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team, is headquartered in Brackley and races under a German licence, with ownership shared equally among Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff as of January 2022. The marque is historically known by the "Silver Arrows" nickname.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor established in 2024 that operates as a second team under Red Bull GmbH's ownership, alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with additional facilities in Milton Keynes, the team represents Red Bull's expansion into a dual-team structure within the championship.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the championship in 2024 as a sister team to Red Bull Racing, both owned by Red Bull GmbH. Based in Faenza with operations near its Milton Keynes-based counterpart, the squad operates as one of two constructors under the Austrian conglomerate's Formula One portfolio.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, operating under an Austrian licence from its English base, emerged as a Formula One competitor in 2005 and has become one of two teams within the Red Bull GmbH motorsport portfolio. The squad operated under Christian Horner's management throughout its two-decade tenure before transitioning to Laurent Mekies' leadership in 2025.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, operating as Atlassian Williams F1 Team in 2026, is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head following the collapse of Williams's prior racing venture. Headquartered on a substantial facility in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team has maintained its presence as a constructor and competitor in Formula One for nearly five decades.
